game.summary: Findings 1-11 fixed (9 needed no change). F1: three admission layers. (a) authorizeEntry refuses neither/both code+createToken and malformed tokens (400) before a seat is reserved, and keeps 426/404/409. (b) filterBy(['code','createToken']); create carries a 128-bit createToken (crypto.getRandomValues in web, node:crypto in test-tools); onCreate stores it, replaces the listing metadata with {code,custom} and refuses token-less creates. (c) onJoin admits one creator-token seat, then only seats with this match's code (404 other code, 403 otherwise). PROTOCOL_VERSION is now 2. New tests/integration/admission.test.ts covers join/joinOrCreate/joinById without a code, with a wrong code and with code+token (exact messages); code-less requests reserving no seat (7 coded players still fill the match); token joinOrCreate always creating; the token never in listings; spent-token replay; the creator getting in and the room still running; and the last-seat race. F2: npm run build ends with node scripts/smoke-build.ts: it loads every workspace export from dist/, starts apps/server/dist/main.js with PORT=0, reads the port from the listening line, waits for /__healthcheck and creates a match via HeadlessClient (SDK), waiting for the creator's ship. Every wait is bounded, the whole run is capped at 90 s, and the server is SIGTERM/SIGKILLed in finally plus exit/signal handlers. F3: MATCHMAKE_INVALID_CRITERIA -> 'That match is full or no longer exists'. F4: frame-tag limitation in docs/architecture.md. F5: apps/web/src/connection.test.ts. The real SDK call showed an unreachable server surfaces as MatchMakeError without a numeric code, not TypeError, so refusalMessage now maps that too. F6: clock test in match.test.ts (frames 60 +/-15 %, patch timer and client patches under 23 Hz). F7: MatchView.renderPosition test. F8: purity test bans transcendental Math with samples. F10: the integration test moves toward the map centre. F11: HEADINGS built once; seaScene uses cssColor. Checks run: npm run typecheck, npm run test:unit (86 pass), npm run test:integration (14 pass, 5 repeats), npm run build (smoke passed) and the full Playwright run (2 pass), all also from npm ci in a clean copy of the worktree. The Playwright JSON report passed workflow check-report (both scenarios ok). Mutation checks: patchRate 1000/60, setFixedTimestep 45, no onJoin admit, token kept in metadata, filterBy code only, and allowing code-less requests each fail at least one new test. The smoke failed with the real ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND when a dist file was missing, and failed after 20 s when the server never listened, leaving no orphan process.
open_assumptions: A malformed code without a token keeps the existing 404 'No match with that code'; only neither/both/malformed-token get 400 'Malformed match request'.
Room-level refusals: 404 NO_SUCH_MATCH for another match's code; new 403 'Joining this match needs its code' for a seat with no code or a foreign or spent token.
onCreate refuses a token-less create (a create with a code, or the joinOrCreate fallback) with Colyseus MATCHMAKE_INVALID_CRITERIA and 'That match is full or no longer exists'.

The protocol-mismatch text changed to 'Protocol version mismatch: client vX, server vY. Reload the page to update.' and echoes only safe integers, so it stays under 100 bytes; tests match /Protocol version mismatch/.

scripts/smoke-build.ts is TypeScript run by Node 24's built-in type stripping (no tsx) and uses the built @pirate-sea-race/test-tools HeadlessClient, which drives @colyseus/sdk; it is typechecked through the root tsconfig include.
The residual joinById seat squatting by someone who knows a roomId (raw HTTP, never connecting, held for the 15 s seat reservation timeout) is documented, not closed, per decisions.md.

MatchRoom.authorizeEntry passes any well-formed createToken, and any code of another live match (which anyone gets by creating their own match). So a caller who knows a roomId can have Colyseus reserve seats (Room._reserveSeat) before MatchRoom.onJoin/admit refuses them, and a caller who never opens the WebSocket holds each seat until the 15 s seatReservationTimeout. A seat reserved and then refused by onJoin is freed before the listing check (listing.clients === 1) and before the 7 coded joins. So this test would also pass if authorizeEntry stopped refusing code-less requests and only the room-level backstop remained. The property is still pinned indirectly: the first admission test asserts code 400 'Malformed match request' for join/joinOrCreate/joinById without a code, and only the static onAuth emits that code. To test the behaviour directly, POST matchmake requests without connecting (for example via client.http or matchMaker.reserveSeatFor-level calls), then assert the listing's clients count and that seven coded players still get in.

inputs.decisions:
# Decisions: skeleton-fixes

From the operator session of 2026-09-24, after the independent review of run skeleton-001 blocked its candidate (general and coverage reviewers, one P1 each).

## Decisions

- This is a follow-up feature on top of skeleton-001's candidate (snapshot `50b14b3`, branch `skeleton/candidate-001`), not a new run of `skeleton`: the lane starts from the reviewed code and changes only what `game-task.md` lists. Reviewers review this diff; the skeleton's own requirements in `features/skeleton/` still apply.
- Scope is findings 1–11 of `game-task.md`: both P1s, the P2s that are cheap to close (3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8) and the operator's code-review findings 10 and 11. Finding 9 is already fixed in this base. The general reviewer's P2 about `allocateCode` exhausting its 16 attempts is deferred.
- Private-match admission has three layers, because Colyseus reserves a seat before any room-level check runs. Checking in the room alone would still let code-less HTTP joins reserve seats and fill a match. The design challenge of run skeleton-fixes-001 (attempt 1) proposed this design.
  - (a) The static `onAuth` (`authorizeEntry`) refuses, before any seat is reserved, a request with neither a well-formed `code` nor a `createToken`, and one with both (400). It keeps its existing checks: protocol version (426), unknown code through `matchMaker.query` (404, "No match with that code"), and full match (409).
  - (b) The room is registered with `filterBy(["code", "createToken"])`. A `create` carries a one-time random `createToken` of at least 128 bits, generated with the platform's crypto API outside the pure packages. Colyseus copies `filterBy` fields from the create options into the listing's metadata, so `onCreate` must replace the metadata (`setMatchmaking`) so it never keeps the token. A request carrying a token then matches no existing listing: `join` fails, and `joinOrCreate` can only create.
  - (c) The room's `onJoin` (or instance `onAuth`) is the backstop, which also covers `joinById`. It admits exactly one seat carrying the token stored in `onCreate` (the creator's); every other seat must carry `code` equal to `this.state.code`.
  - What remains: someone who already knows a roomId (a current or former member) can reserve seats through `joinById` until they expire. `docs/architecture.md` records this.
- The join options change, so `PROTOCOL_VERSION` goes from 1 to 2; tests and the HUD read the constant, not a literal.
- The build output is proven inside the existing `build` check: `npm run build` finishes with a smoke script under `scripts/` that runs the built server on a free port, creates a match through `@colyseus/sdk` and stops it. The policy stays unchanged, and `build` runs before `browser` in the verifier's order.
- The generic matchmaker failure (`MATCHMAKE_INVALID_CRITERIA`) is shown as "That match is full or no longer exists"; "No match with that code" is kept for the server's own 404 refusal.

- Refusal messages stay under 100 bytes. A refusal from the room arrives after the WebSocket opens and may travel as a close reason, which WebSocket caps at 123 bytes. Integration tests assert the exact text.
- The build smoke script runs the server with `PORT=0` and reads the port from its "listening" line. It limits every wait and kills the server on every path, so a failure shows its real error instead of the build check's 600 s timeout, and no orphan disturbs the browser check.

## Assumptions

- In Colyseus 0.18.16, a seat reservation returns only `name`, `sessionId`, `roomId` and `processId` (`buildSeatReservation` in `@colyseus/core`), not listing metadata. A reservation therefore does not reveal the code; the risk the layers close is seat squatting.
- The room's `onJoin(client, options)` or instance `onAuth` can refuse a seat by throwing, and the client receives the error's message.
- Frame tags keep their current meaning in this feature: checked against the 30-frame future window, then applied from the next step. Only the documentation changes.
- `tests/reporters/testSummary.ts` stays registered in `vitest.config.ts`; new test files need nothing extra to be counted.
- The lane may add test files anywhere under its owned paths and may adjust existing tests only where a finding says they are wrong (finding 10, and literals of the protocol version).

## Deferred

- `allocateCode` failing after 16 attempts (reachable only with extreme numbers of live rooms).
- Frame-accurate input application, client prediction and reconciliation: the combat spike.
- Replacing the `colyseus` meta-package with `@colyseus/core`, `@colyseus/ws-transport` and `@colyseus/schema` (it would drop `uWebSockets.js` fetched from GitHub during `npm ci`).
- Matchmaking with a driver other than the local one (Redis), whose metadata filtering must be rechecked.
- Vitest support in md-manager's verifier (`text_test_counts` in `workflow/checks.py`); it belongs to md-manager, not this repository.

concerns.message: Layer (b) says onCreate must 'replace the metadata (setMatchmaking)'. In Colyseus 0.16/0.17, setMatchmaking({metadata}) goes through setMetadata, which merges field by field into the existing listing.metadata. It does not replace it. If 0.18 behaves the same way, `setMatchmaking({ metadata: { code, custom } })` (MatchRoom.ts:86, unchanged) keeps a createToken that filterBy copied from the create options.
concerns.consequence: The acceptance test 'listing metadata never contains the token' fails, or a worker who tests only for a value quietly ships a listing that still carries the token. The fix is an explicit delete or overwrite of listing.metadata.createToken. The worker must check the real behaviour, not trust the wording.

concerns.message: The acceptance test 'a joinOrCreate carrying a token creates a new match and never lands in an existing one' is only meaningful if it reuses the creator's own token from an existing match. With a fresh token, no listing can match whether or not the metadata was scrubbed, so the test passes even when layer (b) is broken.
concerns.consequence: A test that always passes stands as proof of layer (b). A listing that keeps its token (see the merge concern) would not be caught by this test.

concerns.message: 'join, joinOrCreate and joinById without a code … are refused with the exact short message' only makes sense for requests carrying neither a code nor a token. Static onAuth cannot tell the methods apart. So `join {createToken}` passes layer (a) and fails with Colyseus's generic MATCHMAKE_INVALID_CRITERIA text, and `joinOrCreate {createToken}` is meant to create.
concerns.consequence: A worker who reads 'without a code' literally writes a token-only join test that expects the project's message and can never pass. They then either burn time or add method detection that the design does not call for.

concerns.message: The browser has to generate the createToken. `crypto.randomUUID()` gives only 122 random bits, below the required 128, and exists only in secure contexts. `serverEndpoint` uses location.hostname, so the client is meant to work on plain-http LAN hosts too.
concerns.consequence: If the worker uses randomUUID, the token is under the decided strength, and creating a match throws on http://<LAN-IP> playtests while localhost e2e stays green. The web and test-tools code should use crypto.getRandomValues (web) and randomBytes (node) for 16 or more bytes.

concerns.message: Room-level refusals and joinById outcomes are new SDK error shapes: a room error after the WebSocket opens, and MATCHMAKE_INVALID_ROOM_ID. Finding 5's unit tests for refusalMessage will probably hand-build error objects. The unreachable-server branch depends on `error instanceof TypeError`, which holds only if @colyseus/sdk 0.18.4 does not wrap fetch failures.
concerns.consequence: The unit tests can pass against made-up error shapes while the real SDK's errors take a different branch, for example a wrapped network error showing a raw message instead of 'Cannot reach the match server'. They should use the SDK's exported ServerError and ErrorCode, and one integration assertion should point refusalMessage at a closed port.

concerns.message: The smoke script's child server outlives the script unless it is killed explicitly. On Linux a spawned child is not killed when its parent exits or throws. SIGTERM goes through Colyseus gracefullyShutdown, which can wait on rooms to dispose. @colyseus/sdk is not a root dependency; it resolves from scripts/ only because npm hoists it from apps/web and test-tools.
concerns.consequence: If an uncaught SDK rejection skips the finally block, or SIGTERM hangs, a server stays running during the browser check and the build step reports a timeout instead of the real error. The script needs a timed SIGTERM with a SIGKILL fallback and a synchronous process.on('exit') kill. It should also forward the server's stderr on failure. It should import PROTOCOL_VERSION from the built protocol package rather than hard-coding it.

concerns.message: Refusal messages are required to stay under 100 bytes, but protocolMismatchMessage embeds the client-supplied version. For a request with no protocolVersion it produces '…speaks vundefined…', which is 106 bytes. Under layer (a), a malformed code without a token becomes 400 instead of today's 404 'No match with that code', so a player who types a short code gets the malformed-request text.
concerns.consequence: A worker who asserts the byte limit on every refusal, including the new code-less requests, finds it broken by an existing message. Players who mistype a code see a less helpful error. Cap or omit the reflected version, and keep malformed-code-without-token on the 404 message.

concerns.message: Finding 6's clock test may show that the base is wrong. It is unclear whether `setFixedTimestep(cb, STEPS_PER_SECOND)` takes a rate or a step length in ms. If it takes ms, the room runs at about 16.7 steps per second and every existing test still passes.
concerns.consequence: Fixing the rate then speeds ships up about 3.6×. That changes how far the finding-10 movement test travels and could affect the e2e two-ships-sync scenario, which is unplanned rework late in the run. Measure it first.

challenge.simpler_alternative: Drop the createToken. Add one custom HTTP route on the Colyseus server (e.g. POST /match) that calls matchMaker.createRoom(MATCH_ROOM, {protocolVersion}) and returns the code. The client, headless client and smoke script then always `join` by code. Every SDK request must carry a well-formed code: static onAuth refuses anything without one (400) and keeps its existing 404/409/426 checks, and the room's onJoin checks options.code === state.code. There is no token, no filterBy on a token, no metadata scrubbing and no one-seat creator exception; filterBy stays ['code']. The cost is a second round-trip for the creator and a join deadline of seatReservationTime before the empty room auto-disposes. decisions.md already settles the three-layer design, and I found nothing that stops it working, so I recommend staying with it. Use this only if the cheap experiment shows layer (b) or (c) cannot work as described.
challenge.cheap_experiment: Spend about 15 minutes on the base commit before any worker starts. Write a throwaway script run with tsx --conditions=@pirate-sea-race/source that starts startGameServer({port:0}) with filterBy(['code','createToken']). (1) `create` with {protocolVersion, createToken:T}, then print matchMaker.query({name})[0].metadata after onCreate. This shows whether filterBy copies the token into metadata and whether setMatchmaking merges or replaces. (2) `joinOrCreate` with the same T and compare roomIds. (3) Temporarily throw new ServerError(404,'No match with that code') from onJoin and print the SDK rejection's code, message and class. (4) Sample room.state.frame over 2 s and count onStateChange calls. If (3) loses the message, layer (c) must move to the instance onAuth or the design should switch to the alternative. If (1) shows a merge, the worker must delete the token explicitly. If (4) is not about 60 frames and at most 20 patches per second, the clock fix and its effects on tests become part of the plan.

# Task: game

## Goal

Fix what the independent review of run skeleton-001 found in the walking skeleton on this branch: private matches must be unjoinable without their code, a check must prove the server runs from its build output, and the review's test gaps must be closed. Everything else about the skeleton stays as it is.

## Context

- This branch starts from skeleton-001's reviewed candidate (the `skeleton` feature: `features/skeleton/game-task.md` and `features/skeleton/decisions.md` still describe what the skeleton must do, and all of it still applies). Read `docs/architecture.md` first, then the files named below.
- The verifier runs `npm ci` in a clean worktree, then `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test:unit`, `npm run test:integration`, `npm run build` and `npx --no-install playwright test --config=tests/e2e/playwright.config.ts`. Each must pass from a clean checkout.
- The verifier reads unit and integration test counts only from a Node test-runner summary (`# tests N`, `# pass N`, `# fail N`, `# skipped N`). `tests/reporters/testSummary.ts`, registered in `vitest.config.ts`, prints Vitest's counts in that form. Keep it registered; without it every passing test run is refused as "no passing test evidence".
- Playwright's Chromium for `@playwright/test` 1.63.0 is installed and shared read-only; never run `playwright install`.

Review findings to fix (reviewer, severity):

1. (general, P1) `authorizeEntry` in `apps/server/src/MatchRoom.ts` treats any request without `code` as a create. Colyseus 0.18 exposes `join`, `joinOrCreate` and `joinById` over its HTTP matchmaker too. A `join` with only `{protocolVersion}` gets no `filterBy` filter, so it seats the caller in an arbitrary open private match, and the room never checks the code itself.
2. (coverage, P1) No check starts the server from its build output. `npm run build` only compiles; the integration tests and the Playwright web server run the TypeScript sources through the `@pirate-sea-race/source` condition. A broken `dist/` (including the workspace packages' `default` → `./dist/*.js` exports) passes all five checks.
3. (general, P2) Two joins racing for the eighth seat: the loser gets Colyseus's `MATCHMAKE_INVALID_CRITERIA`, which `refusalMessage` in `apps/web/src/connection.ts` shows as "No match with that code" although the match exists.
4. (general, P2) `InputGate` uses an input's frame tag only for the future-window check; accepted input applies from the next step whatever frame it names. Acceptable without prediction, but undocumented.
5. (coverage, P2) Only the headless SDK path checks refusal messages; `refusalMessage` and its display in `#join-error` have no test for the protocol-mismatch and full-match refusals.
6. (coverage, P2) Nothing tests the room's clock: a misread `setFixedTimestep` argument or `patchRate` would pass every test.
7. (coverage, P2) Interpolation is tested only inside `SnapshotBuffer`; nothing proves the client draws interpolated rather than latest positions.
8. (coverage, P2) The decision that the step function uses no floating-point transcendental functions is not enforced by any test.

Found by the operator's code review of the same candidate:

9. Already fixed in this base: `mapBounds` returns `widthTiles * subUnitsPerTile - 1`, and `simulation.test.ts` ("clamps ships to the map bounds") checks that a clamped ship lies on the last tile. Change nothing for it.
10. The integration test "lets two clients join the same code and see the same authoritative movement" always holds `moveX: 1` for 600 ms; from the rightmost spawn slot that leaves a margin of about one world step before the edge clamps it. Move toward the map centre, as the e2e test does.
11. `headingOf` in `packages/simulation/src/step.ts` builds its lookup object on every call; `apps/web/src/seaScene.ts` formats the slot colour by hand instead of using `cssColor` from `matchView.ts`.

## Constraints

- Change only what these findings need; keep the file layout, naming and patterns of the existing code (tagged results at trust boundaries, zod schemas as the source of types, injected dependencies, doc comments citing spec sections).
- The pure packages stay pure (`CLAUDE.md`). Keep every existing test passing; change a test only where a finding says it is wrong.
- Keep the policy's check commands and the two browser scenario ids unchanged. Never change `docs/spec.docx`, `docs/spec.md` or `features/`.

From the operator session of 2026-09-24, after the independent review of run skeleton-001 blocked its candidate (general and coverage reviewers, one P1 each).

## Decisions

- This is a follow-up feature on top of skeleton-001's candidate (snapshot `50b14b3`, branch `skeleton/candidate-001`), not a new run of `skeleton`: the lane starts from the reviewed code and changes only what `game-task.md` lists. Reviewers review this diff; the skeleton's own requirements in `features/skeleton/` still apply.
- Scope is findings 1–11 of `game-task.md`: both P1s, the P2s that are cheap to close (3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8) and the operator's code-review findings 10 and 11. Finding 9 is already fixed in this base. The general reviewer's P2 about `allocateCode` exhausting its 16 attempts is deferred.
- Private-match admission has three layers, because Colyseus reserves a seat before any room-level check runs. Checking in the room alone would still let code-less HTTP joins reserve seats and fill a match. The design challenge of run skeleton-fixes-001 (attempt 1) proposed this design.
  - (a) The static `onAuth` (`authorizeEntry`) refuses, before any seat is reserved, a request with neither a well-formed `code` nor a `createToken`, and one with both (400). It keeps its existing checks: protocol version (426), unknown code through `matchMaker.query` (404, "No match with that code"), and full match (409).
  - (b) The room is registered with `filterBy(["code", "createToken"])`. A `create` carries a one-time random `createToken` of at least 128 bits, generated with the platform's crypto API outside the pure packages. Colyseus copies `filterBy` fields from the create options into the listing's metadata, so `onCreate` must replace the metadata (`setMatchmaking`) so it never keeps the token. A request carrying a token then matches no existing listing: `join` fails, and `joinOrCreate` can only create.
  - (c) The room's `onJoin` (or instance `onAuth`) is the backstop, which also covers `joinById`. It admits exactly one seat carrying the token stored in `onCreate` (the creator's); every other seat must carry `code` equal to `this.state.code`.
  - What remains: someone who already knows a roomId (a current or former member) can reserve seats through `joinById` until they expire. `docs/architecture.md` records this.
- The join options change, so `PROTOCOL_VERSION` goes from 1 to 2; tests and the HUD read the constant, not a literal.
- The build output is proven inside the existing `build` check: `npm run build` finishes with a smoke script under `scripts/` that runs the built server on a free port, creates a match through `@colyseus/sdk` and stops it. The policy stays unchanged, and `build` runs before `browser` in the verifier's order.
- The generic matchmaker failure (`MATCHMAKE_INVALID_CRITERIA`) is shown as "That match is full or no longer exists"; "No match with that code" is kept for the server's own 404 refusal.

- Refusal messages stay under 100 bytes. A refusal from the room arrives after the WebSocket opens and may travel as a close reason, which WebSocket caps at 123 bytes. Integration tests assert the exact text.
- The build smoke script runs the server with `PORT=0` and reads the port from its "listening" line. It limits every wait and kills the server on every path, so a failure shows its real error instead of the build check's 600 s timeout, and no orphan disturbs the browser check.

## Assumptions

- In Colyseus 0.18.16, a seat reservation returns only `name`, `sessionId`, `roomId` and `processId` (`buildSeatReservation` in `@colyseus/core`), not listing metadata. A reservation therefore does not reveal the code; the risk the layers close is seat squatting.
- The room's `onJoin(client, options)` or instance `onAuth` can refuse a seat by throwing, and the client receives the error's message.
- Frame tags keep their current meaning in this feature: checked against the 30-frame future window, then applied from the next step. Only the documentation changes.
- `tests/reporters/testSummary.ts` stays registered in `vitest.config.ts`; new test files need nothing extra to be counted.
- The lane may add test files anywhere under its owned paths and may adjust existing tests only where a finding says they are wrong (finding 10, and literals of the protocol version).

## Deferred

- `allocateCode` failing after 16 attempts (reachable only with extreme numbers of live rooms).
- Frame-accurate input application, client prediction and reconciliation: the combat spike.
- Replacing the `colyseus` meta-package with `@colyseus/core`, `@colyseus/ws-transport` and `@colyseus/schema` (it would drop `uWebSockets.js` fetched from GitHub during `npm ci`).

- Vitest support in md-manager's verifier (`text_test_counts` in `workflow/checks.py`); it belongs to md-manager, not this repository.

handoff.summary: Findings 1-11 fixed (9 needed no change). F1: three admission layers. (a) authorizeEntry refuses neither/both code+createToken and malformed tokens (400) before a seat is reserved, and keeps 426/404/409. (b) filterBy(['code','createToken']); create carries a 128-bit createToken (crypto.getRandomValues in web, node:crypto in test-tools); onCreate stores it, replaces the listing metadata with {code,custom} and refuses token-less creates. (c) onJoin admits one creator-token seat, then only seats with this match's code (404 other code, 403 otherwise). PROTOCOL_VERSION is now 2. New tests/integration/admission.test.ts covers join/joinOrCreate/joinById without a code, with a wrong code and with code+token (exact messages); code-less requests reserving no seat (7 coded players still fill the match); token joinOrCreate always creating; the token never in listings; spent-token replay; the creator getting in and the room still running; and the last-seat race. F2: npm run build ends with node scripts/smoke-build.ts: it loads every workspace export from dist/, starts apps/server/dist/main.js with PORT=0, reads the port from the listening line, waits for /__healthcheck and creates a match via HeadlessClient (SDK), waiting for the creator's ship. Every wait is bounded, the whole run is capped at 90 s, and the server is SIGTERM/SIGKILLed in finally plus exit/signal handlers. F3: MATCHMAKE_INVALID_CRITERIA -> 'That match is full or no longer exists'. F4: frame-tag limitation in docs/architecture.md. F5: apps/web/src/connection.test.ts. The real SDK call showed an unreachable server surfaces as MatchMakeError without a numeric code, not TypeError, so refusalMessage now maps that too. F6: clock test in match.test.ts (frames 60 +/-15 %, patch timer and client patches under 23 Hz). F7: MatchView.renderPosition test. F8: purity test bans transcendental Math with samples. F10: the integration test moves toward the map centre. F11: HEADINGS built once; seaScene uses cssColor. Checks run: npm run typecheck, npm run test:unit (86 pass), npm run test:integration (14 pass, 5 repeats), npm run build (smoke passed) and the full Playwright run (2 pass), all also from npm ci in a clean copy of the worktree. The Playwright JSON report passed workflow check-report (both scenarios ok). Mutation checks: patchRate 1000/60, setFixedTimestep 45, no onJoin admit, token kept in metadata, filterBy code only, and allowing code-less requests each fail at least one new test.
